references.text: Jesus takes a cup during the Passover meal, gives thanks, hands it to the disciples, and says that they should all drink from it because it represents his blood, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins. This parallels the action and words Jesus uses in Mark 14:23.

During the Passover meal, Jesus takes a cup, gives thanks, and says that the cup is the new covenant in his blood, which is poured out for them. This resembles the event and words in Mark 14:23, where Jesus shares the cup with the disciples.

Paul describes how Jesus, at the Lord's Supper, took the cup after the meal, gave thanks, and said that this cup is the new covenant in his blood. This is done in remembrance of him and mirrors the event in Mark 14:23.

The prophecy that the Messiah will pour out his life to death and be counted among transgressors points forward to Jesus' sacrifice, which includes the action with the cup in Mark 14:23, symbolizing his blood poured out for many.
The expression of lifting the cup of salvation and calling on the name of the Lord in gratitude can be seen as a precursor to the Lord's Supper cup, which Jesus lifts in thanksgiving in Mark 14:23.
